goal: Use Python list and dictionary comprehensions to transform and filter data.

criteria.outcome: Construct and explain list comprehensions that transform and filter an iterable.
Construct and explain dictionary comprehensions that derive key-value pairs from an iterable.

items.prompt: Write one Python list-comprehension expression that doubles each value in [2, 5, 8].
items.rationale: A list comprehension applies the expression before the for clause to each selected input value.

items.prompt: Write one list comprehension that keeps only positive values from [-3, 0, 2, 5].
items.rationale: An if clause can filter which iterable elements contribute results.

items.answer: [x**2 for x in range(7) if x % 2 == 0]
items.prompt: Write one list comprehension that returns the squares of the even numbers produced by range(7).
items.rationale: The comprehension combines a transformation with a filtering condition.

items.prompt: Write one list comprehension that returns lengths of words longer than three characters from ["cat", "tiger", "ox", "horse"].
items.rationale: This delayed item requires both filtering and transformation in a new item family.

items.prompt: Write one dictionary comprehension mapping each number in (2, 3, 4) to its square.
items.rationale: A dictionary comprehension supplies both key and value expressions before the for clause.

items.prompt: Write one dictionary comprehension mapping each word in ["ant", "bear"] to its length.
items.rationale: The key and value expressions may be derived independently from each selected element.

items.prompt: Write one dictionary comprehension mapping each name in ["Ada", "Linus", "Guido"] to the length of that name.
items.rationale: The task independently checks construction of key-value results from each iterable element.

items.prompt: Write one dictionary comprehension mapping each number in range(1, 5) to its cube.
items.rationale: This delayed parallel family checks retained dictionary-comprehension construction.

lessons.objective: Create a list comprehension from an iterable, transformation expression, and optional filter.
lessons.title: Transform and filter with list comprehensions

worked_examples.text: `[x * 2 for x in [1, 2, 3]]` creates `[2, 4, 6]` by transforming each input value.
`[x for x in [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] if x >= 0]` creates `[0, 1, 2]` by filtering the iterable.

lessons.objective: Create a dictionary comprehension that derives a key and value for each selected input item.
lessons.title: Create mappings with dictionary comprehensions

maintenance_tasks.prompt: Write one list comprehension that returns uppercase versions of words longer than two characters from ["a", "bee", "code"].
maintenance_tasks.rationale: A fresh maintenance family combines filtering and transformation.

maintenance_tasks.prompt: Write one dictionary comprehension mapping each word in ["red", "blue"] to its uppercase form.
maintenance_tasks.rationale: A fresh maintenance family checks retained key-value construction.

transfer_tasks.answer: {n: n**2 for n in range(8) if n % 2 == 1}
transfer_tasks.prompt: In one dictionary comprehension, map each odd number produced by range(8) to its square.
transfer_tasks.rationale: This combines dictionary construction with a filter in a context not used in instruction.

transfer_tasks.answer: {w: len(w) for w in ["sun", "planet", "star", "galaxy"] if len(w) > 3}
transfer_tasks.prompt: In one dictionary comprehension, map each word longer than three characters in ["sun", "planet", "star", "galaxy"] to its length.
transfer_tasks.rationale: This combines filtering with derived dictionary values on strings.

tutor_probes.prompt: Write a list comprehension that keeps even numbers from range(6).
Write a list comprehension that keeps numbers greater than 2 from [1,2,3,4].

ABSTAINED.content: The response is not correct, but the cause is not established. Reconstruct the comprehension as output expression, `for` clause, then any filter condition.

DEFAULT.content: Identify the output expression first, then the iterable in the `for` clause, then decide whether a filtering `if` clause is required.

FILTER_OMITTED.content: A filtering comprehension needs an `if` clause after the `for` clause to decide which input elements contribute results.
FILTER_OMITTED.hypothesis_content: Your answer may be missing the filtering part. Check whether an `if` clause is needed after the `for` clause.
